title: Administrative units: which users can a delegated administrator manage?
summary: The page passes: Microsoft's documentation supports its administrative paths, commands, licensing and scope restrictions. The corrected explanations of restricted management and Entra role precedence are supported, and targeted searches found no documented automation for the two Purview control gaps.

claims.claim: Create a unit in the Microsoft Entra admin center at Entra ID > Roles & admins > Admin units > Add.
claims.quote:
Browse to **Entra ID** > **Roles & admins** > **Admin units**.
3. Select **Add**.

claims.quote: The PolicyRBACScopes parameter specifies the administrative units to assign to the policy. A valid value is the Microsoft Entra ObjectID (GUID value) of the administrative unit. You can specify multiple values separated by commas.

claims.claim: An administrative unit is a Microsoft Entra ID resource container.
claims.quote: An administrative unit is a Microsoft Entra resource that can be a container for other Microsoft Entra resources.

claims.claim: An Entra administrative unit can contain only users, groups or devices.
claims.quote: An administrative unit can contain only users, groups, or devices.

claims.claim: An Entra role assigned with unit scope applies only when managing the unit's members.
claims.quote: When a Microsoft Entra role is assigned at the scope of an administrative unit, role permissions apply only when managing members of the administrative unit itself, and don't apply to tenant-wide settings or configurations.

claims.claim: Units permit regional or departmental delegation without tenant-wide administration.
claims.quote: You could, for example, use administrative units to delegate the [Helpdesk Administrator](permissions-reference#helpdesk-administrator) role to regional support specialists, so they can manage users only in the region that they support.
